/findings.body: The diff claims `TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID` and `TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are the names read by `server::auth::AppAuth::from_env`, and that the old `TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_*` names were never read. I was unable to look up the source of `AppAuth::from_env` to confirm this (the search tool was unavailable on this deployment). If the claim is correct this is a good fix; if the binary actually reads `TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_*` (or reads both), renaming to the un-read names and making them required (`:?`) would break authentication for every deployment — the old names now silently vanish and the new ones error on startup if unset. Someone who can read `src/server/auth*` or grep the binary should confirm `from_env` reads `TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID` / `TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` before merging.
/findings.existing_code:
TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID: ${TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID:?set the GitHub App id}
      TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY:?set the GitHub App private key}
/findings.title: Verify env var names match AppAuth::from_env before merging

value.summary: The diff adds forwarded API keys, renames the GitHub App env vars to match what the binary reads, and mounts the config file. I could not confirm the central claim — that `AppAuth::from_env` reads `TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID`/`TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` — because the source search was unavailable; if that claim is wrong, making those vars required will break deployment for everyone.
